name: Universal basic income
what: Regular cash to everyone, no conditions.
funding: General taxation or new taxes on capital, land or carbon
evidence: Many trials of cash, none of a full national UBI; work falls a little, wellbeing rises.
risk: Cost: a payment big enough to matter is very expensive.

name: Negative income tax
what: An income floor through the tax system that tapers as earnings rise.
evidence: Four randomised US experiments, 1968–1982, plus Canada's Mincome.
risk: The taper acts like a high tax rate on extra earnings.

name: Citizen dividends and wealth funds
what: A share of the returns on a commonly owned asset, paid to every resident.
evidence: Four decades of Alaska data; no fall in employment.
risk: Small and volatile unless the fund is very large.

name: Broad ownership and data dividends
what: Endowments at birth, employee ownership, public stakes, payment for data.
funding: Public endowments, firms' equity, platform revenues
evidence: Good evidence on employee ownership; baby bonds and data dividends are new or untested.
risk: Concentrates risk, or stays too small to replace wages.

name: Universal basic services
what: Free essentials such as housing, local transport and digital access.
evidence: Proposals and costings; rich evidence on single services, little on the full package.
risk: Does not give people cash or ownership, so it does not restore economic agency.

name: Job guarantee
what: A public offer of paid work for anyone who wants it.
evidence: Randomised and quasi-experimental evidence from India and Austria.
risk: Keeps income tied to work, the link post-labor thinkers expect to break.
